title: March of the Machine Promos: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Her blades were twin beacons, calling the worthy to glory and the wretched to despair.
"We sailed to Ixalan guided by a promise—the Age of Everflowing Blood. No machine will take that from us."
She was hope incarnate, an incandescent bulwark against the tide of machines.
"*Compleat* the faith, *compleat* the god." —Ajani Goldmane
"*Compleat* the god, *compleat* the plane." —Ajani Goldmane
The weight of Phyrexia crashed down upon Gobakhan, but the will of its people endured.
When the sun falters and the seas disperse, when the wilds wither and the forges go cold, when death itself succumbs, she endures.
"One path. Many feet."
"Let the light scour away your imperfect flesh." —Heliod
Yuta Takahashi, World Champion XXVII
No professors, no grades, no room for mistakes.
"At last, I am *compleat*."
Wrenn reached out to Teferi through the Blind Eternities, and an impossible connection flared across the vast emptiness.
Ayara cherished her new machine servitors just as much as she once did her many suitors: not at all.
"All worlds will know perfection." —Elesh Norn
The eerie magic animating Innistrad's zombies rendered them immune to phyresis, making them crucial to the plane's defense.
The contagion spreads and the Multiverse quakes.
The rest of the Gatewatch retreated. Chandra and Wrenn went in blazing.
The warriors of Kaldheim burned the soul of their world to keep it out of Phyrexia's hands.
The crystal landslide stirred over the shattered forms of the Machine Legion vanguard, and then it rose and rearranged itself into an avenging colossus.
"The Phyrexians are fools if they believe they can weather such a storm." —Sarkhan Vol
"Zendikar must be broken before it can be saved."
"The end is always nigh. Let's have some fun!"
Her warning raced through the roots and rivers of Ixalan: prepare for war.
Unleashed on new worlds, the Phyrexians were driven by a simple imperative: spread and conquer.
Phyrexia's largest goliaths stormed Ikoria, ready to challenge the world's great monsters. Zilortha was unimpressed.
"Careful. Its vision is based on fear, and it can smell movement . . . or something like that." —Gregor, amateur zoologist
Shandalar's wild magic stripped away the unnatural Phyrexian carapaces, reclaiming the true forms hidden underneath.
Freed from the Underworld, the World Eater resumed his endless feast with reckless enthusiasm.
"The Tree was the heart of our world. It made me what I am and pulled me back from the brink of death. I won't allow it to be forgotten." —Esika, god of the Tree
Angry ghosts poured through and pummeled the Invasion Tree, filling the heavens with the rhythms of war.
When the Invasion Tree reached the Underworld, it found only teeth and fury.

"I've heard much about you from my daughter," Multani rumbled. "There was a time when I'd balk at your aid, phantom, but she has shown me the merit in Urborg's strange ways." "Gnshhagghkkapphribbit," replied Yargle.
